data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 2121 experienced an overall net deterioration of GBP 3.7 million on prior years' provisions in 2019. This was primarily driven by deteriorations in third party liability, energy, and pecuniary loss accounts, which were partially offset by favorable development in reinsurance acceptances. Specific events contributing to prior year strengthening included increased medium-sized losses in the 2017 casualty account related to California wildfires and the MGM shooting, as well as man-made losses from 2018 such as fires at Macy's and Brazilian warehouses (cargo account) and an increase in political risk losses from 2018. Conversely, reserves for 2016 and prior years developed satisfactorily, generating a surplus of GBP 4.4 million.
raw_causal_phrases: An overall deterioration of GBP 3.7 million on prior years' provisions was experienced during the year.
Deteriorations of GBP 11.5 million on third party liability
offset by an improvement of GBP 17.5 million on reinsurance acceptances.

The 2017 year also required a strengthening of the reserves within the casualty account, in line with the market, following increased medium sized losses from the California wildfires and the MGM shooting in the US.

From a man-made loss perspective the largest losses remain as stated last year; being from fires at a Macy's warehouse in the US and in a Brazilian warehouse. Both of these losses emanated from the cargo account.
Also, an increase in political risk losses was seen in respect of business incepting during the 2018 year of account.
Reserves in respect of the 2016 and prior years of account continue to develop satisfactorily, generating a surplus of GBP 4.4 million during the 2019 calendar year.

data.data_quality_notes: The prior year development figure of GBP 3.7m is stated as an "overall deterioration" but is likely a net figure, as the sum of the provided LOB movements (GBP 1.7m) does not match it. The claims development triangles (gross and net) are incomplete in the provided OCR text, preventing their use for prior year development calculation. Reinsurance to Close (RITC) premium of GBP 118.669m for the 2016 year of account was received by the 2017 year of account, which would distort any PYD calculation from the claims development triangle if it were available.
